topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory welcome and sets out the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: intrinsic mutations, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental causes of cancer by comparing intrinsic genetic errors and bad luck with environmental exposures and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, illustrated through the etiology and mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental susceptibility cooperate with initiators to facilitate cancer progression.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their real-world risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic delivers the closing summary of the lecture's core themes.
